prompt.context_jp: 「これは…」「私___書いたレシピノートです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私___書いたレシピノートです」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that correctly identifies who wrote the notebook.

feedback.correct_en: The social president's wife is identifying herself as the one who wrote it — 'I'm the one who wrote it.' This is exhaustive/identificational, so が marks the subject within the relative clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make '私' the topic of the main sentence, which conflicts with the structure '私が書いた' (relative clause modifying ノート).

contrast_examples.en: It's the dish I made (I'm the one who made it).

contrast_examples.jp: 私は料理を作りました。
contrast_examples.en: As for me, I made food.

prompt.context_jp: 「メニューを考えてるの___家内なんで」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「メニューを考えてるの___家内なんで」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits — answering 'who thinks up the menu'?

feedback.correct_en: The 'の' nominalizes the clause and は marks it as the topic: 'As for the one who thinks up the menu, it's my wife.' This is a cleft-like structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly force a new-information reading on the nominalized clause itself, which is already serving as the topic being described.

contrast_examples.jp: 料理を作るのは私です。
contrast_examples.en: The one who cooks is me.
I (and no one else) will cook.

prompt.context_jp: 「恐らく ＡＩ___ 1個の売れ残りすら出しません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「恐らく ＡＩ___ 1個の売れ残りすら出しません」
prompt.prompt_en: Haruko is comparing AI to the factory — pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Haruko sets up AI as the topic to describe its characteristic behavior ('as for AI, it won't leave even one unsold'). This is a generic/characterizing statement, so は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal new information or exhaustive listing — but AI has just been under discussion, and this is a general characterization, not identification.

contrast_examples.en: It was AI that made the mistake.

prompt.context_jp: 「社長 午後の出荷数 750のままでいいですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「午後の出荷数___750のままでいいですか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the shipment number.

feedback.correct_en: The employee topicalizes the shipment number to confirm it: 'As for the afternoon shipment number, is 750 OK?' は fits a confirmation question about an existing topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would require a verb that takes it as direct object (none here). が would make the shipment number new information, odd in a confirmation.

contrast_examples.jp: 値段はこのままでいいですか？
contrast_examples.en: Is the price OK as it is?

prompt.context_jp: 「それは 隅田フーズのお弁当___ おいしいからでしょう」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「隅田フーズのお弁当___ おいしいからでしょう」
prompt.prompt_en: Why the profits rose — which particle marks 'bento'?

feedback.correct_en: Within the subordinate clause explaining the cause, が marks the subject of おいしい in a stative description identifying what is delicious ('because Sumida's bento is delicious').
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a からだ/からでしょう cause clause would awkwardly topicalize the bento instead of simply stating the reason.

contrast_examples.jp: 料理がおいしいから人気です。
contrast_examples.en: It's popular because the food is delicious.

contrast_examples.jp: この料理はおいしいです。
contrast_examples.en: This dish is delicious (as for this dish).

prompt.context_jp: 「春子だけ___、機械のような等速で笹の葉を並べ続けている」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「春子だけ___ 機械のような等速で笹の葉を並べ続けている」
prompt.prompt_en: Everyone else is scrambling — which particle fits 'only Haruko'?

feedback.correct_en: With 〜だけ highlighting an exclusive subject ('only Haruko, and no one else'), が gives the exhaustive-listing reading that fits this contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'だけは' would shift to a contrastive topic nuance ('at least Haruko' — as for her alone), weakening the exclusive-identification effect the narrator intends.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼だけは知らなかった。

prompt.context_jp: 「ＡＩ___間違わないんだ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ＡＩ___間違わないんだ」
prompt.prompt_en: Tōkairin's declaration about AI — which particle?

feedback.correct_en: Tōkairin is making a sweeping, characterizing claim about AI as a topic: 'AI doesn't make mistakes.' This generic assertion calls for は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would narrow the meaning to 'it's AI that doesn't make mistakes (unlike X)' — a specific identification that doesn't match his broad declaration of faith.

prompt.context_jp: 「評価が良くなるの___ まごころ弁当であって 隅田フーズじゃない」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「評価が良くなるの___ まごころ弁当であって 隅田フーズじゃない」
prompt.prompt_en: Tōkairin is contrasting bento vs. Sumida Foods — which particle?

feedback.correct_en: The nominalized 'の' is the cleft topic: 'As for what gets a better evaluation, it's the bento, not Sumida Foods.' This は also carries contrastive force.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly re-package the clause as new-information subject, losing the contrastive 'not X, but Y' framing central to Tōkairin's point.

contrast_examples.jp: 評価されるのは商品であって会社じゃない。
contrast_examples.en: What gets evaluated is the product, not the company.

prompt.context_jp: 「弁当を作っているの___ 隅田フーズだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「弁当を作っているの___ 隅田フーズだよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Satonaka counters Tōkairin — which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Another cleft: 'The one making the bento is Sumida Foods.' は marks the nominalized clause as topic while delivering the identificational payoff on 隅田フーズ.
feedback.incorrect_en: が on the nominalized clause would be ungrammatical here — the pattern 〜のは Xだ is the standard cleft structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 料理を作るのは母です。
contrast_examples.en: The one who cooks is my mother.

prompt.context_jp: 「切られるの___ 派遣ではありません あなた方 社員です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「切られるの___ 派遣ではありません」
prompt.prompt_en: Haruko's pointed reversal — which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Cleft with contrast: 'The ones who'll be cut aren't the temps — it's you regulars.' The 〜のは〜ではない pattern is textbook contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が wouldn't fit the cleft/contrast frame; the sentence explicitly denies one candidate and asserts another.

contrast_examples.en: The one at fault isn't me.

prompt.context_jp: 「空___うっすらと雲に覆われ、予報どおりなら午後は雨のはずだった」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「空___うっすらと雲に覆われ」
prompt.prompt_en: Opening scene-setting description — which particle?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator takes 'the sky' as the scene topic to describe its state. Characterizing descriptions of the backdrop use は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the sky suddenly-introduced new information, which doesn't fit this calm, panning scene-setting voice.

prompt.context_jp: 「昼過ぎ、約束を裏切ったかのように空___暗くなり、大粒の雨___窓を叩き始めた」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「空___暗くなり、大粒の雨___窓を叩き始めた」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fills both blanks as the weather turns?

feedback.correct_en: Both clauses describe sudden changes/events — the sky darkening, raindrops starting. New-event descriptions take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame them as pre-established topics, flattening the dramatic turn the narrator wants to convey.

prompt.context_jp: 「違います 隅田フーズ___ 切られるのではありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「隅田フーズ___ 切られるのではありません」
prompt.prompt_en: Haruko reframes who is 'cutting' whom — pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Sumida Foods is the topic Haruko is re-characterizing, with contrastive force: 'As for Sumida Foods — they are NOT being cut.' Negation-with-contrast strongly favors は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight Sumida Foods as a newly identified subject of a negation, which clashes with Haruko's deliberate reframing of a known party.

contrast_examples.en: He is not the bad one (contrast).

prompt.context_jp: 「弁当の出荷数を割り出し 御社___ ご提案しています」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「御社___ご提案しています」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the recipient of the proposal?

feedback.correct_en: The president is proposing TO S&F (indirect recipient of 提案する). The goal/recipient of a verb of giving/suggesting takes に.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mean 'at' S&F (location). を would make S&F the direct object of 提案, which is ungrammatical.

prompt.context_jp: 「ＡＩは 分刻み___ 天候の変化を考慮して 出荷数を決定しています」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「分刻み___天候の変化を考慮して」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle expresses the manner 'minute by minute'?

feedback.correct_en: で marks manner/means here — 'on a minute-by-minute basis.' 分刻みで is the fixed way to express this interval granularity.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would suggest a point in time; を would require a transitive verb taking 分刻み as object.

prompt.context_jp: 「雨のち晴れです ___ 晴れます！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「雨のち晴れです ___ 晴れます！」
prompt.prompt_en: Haruko insists sun is coming — which adverb fits?

feedback.correct_en: じき means 'soon/shortly' — a slightly literary adverb that fits Haruko's confident weather-forecaster register.
feedback.incorrect_en: もう晴れます would imply 'already clearing' (not quite right — it hasn't started yet). まだ晴れます is ungrammatical in context.

prompt.context_jp: 「しかし___も積もれば山となるで、月末には廃棄率がはっきりと下がり」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___も積もれば山となる」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the proverb about small things adding up.

feedback.correct_en: 塵も積もれば山となる ('even dust piled up becomes a mountain') is the set proverb for small efforts compounding.
feedback.incorrect_en: 砂 and 水 don't form the standard proverb; the fixed form uses 塵.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Many a little makes a mickle.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.

prompt.context_jp: 「5時なので このまま ___させていただきます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「このまま ___させていただきます」
prompt.prompt_en: Haruko leaves exactly at 5 — pick the business expression.

feedback.correct_en: 直帰 ('go straight home from an outside site, without returning to the office') is the precise business term for Haruko's situation at the factory.
feedback.incorrect_en: 帰宅 just means 'go home' generally; 退社 means 'leave the company (for the day or permanently)' — neither captures the 'not returning to HQ' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 直行直帰で営業します。
contrast_examples.en: Work sales going direct both ways (no office stop).

prompt.context_jp: 「そこで働く人たちのことを 同じ___の飯を食う仲間だって 思ってるからな」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「同じ___の飯を食う仲間」
prompt.prompt_en: Tōkairin's set phrase about workplace bonds.

feedback.correct_en: 同じ釜の飯を食う ('eating rice from the same pot') is the fixed idiom for close workplace/group comradeship.
feedback.incorrect_en: 鍋 and 皿 don't form the idiom — the image is specifically rice cooked in one kama.

contrast_examples.jp: 同じ釜の飯を食った仲間。
contrast_examples.en: Comrades who ate from the same pot.

contrast_examples.jp: 一つ屋根の下で暮らす。

prompt.context_jp: 「___足らずで 申し訳ありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___足らずで 申し訳ありません」
prompt.prompt_en: Haruko's formal apology after the forecast fails.

feedback.correct_en: 力不足/力足らず ('lacking in ability') is the stock humble apology for failing to deliver.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手足らず and 気足らず aren't standard set expressions for apologizing about professional shortcomings.

contrast_examples.en: It was due to my lack of ability.

prompt.context_jp: 「Ｓ＆Ｆという デカいだけが取り柄の___に 無理に乗っていただく必要は ありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「デカいだけが取り柄の___」
prompt.prompt_en: Haruko's metaphor for S&F — pick the noun.

feedback.correct_en: 泥舟 ('mud boat') is the classic metaphor for a doomed vessel that will sink — fitting Haruko's warning that S&F only looks safe.
feedback.incorrect_en: 小舟 is contrasted a sentence later as Sumida's humble but seaworthy craft. 大船 ('big ship') with 乗る is the positive idiom for feeling secure, the opposite of what Haruko means.

contrast_examples.jp: 大船に乗ったつもりで。
contrast_examples.en: Rest assured (as if on a big ship).

prompt.context_jp: 「ちょっと 間が悪かったみたいね みんな 忙しそう また___ことにするわね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「また___ことにするわね」
prompt.prompt_en: Kayo plans to come back another time — pick the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 出直す means 'come back another time / start over' — the natural choice when the timing is bad.
feedback.incorrect_en: 出かけてくる is just 'go out,' and 出発する is for starting a journey — neither fits 'try again later.'

contrast_examples.jp: ちょっと出かけてきます。
contrast_examples.en: I'm stepping out for a bit.

prompt.context_jp: 「“泳ぎださないと ___” …と警告したはずです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「泳ぎださないと ___」
prompt.prompt_en: Haruko's earlier warning — pick the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 溺れる ('drown') completes the metaphor: if you don't start swimming, you drown. It pairs most naturally with the active 泳ぎだす.
feedback.incorrect_en: 流れる (be carried away) and 沈む (sink) are related but less precise — 'drown' is the direct consequence of not swimming.

contrast_examples.en: You'll drown if you don't swim.

prompt.context_jp: Haruko leaves the factory at exactly 5pm during a crisis.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural coming from Haruko the dispatch pro?

choices.text: 5時なので このまま 直帰させていただきます
5時ですので 家に帰らせていただきたいです

feedback.correct_en: The actual line uses the fixed business expression 直帰させていただきます — crisp, polite, and work-specific.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is casual and inappropriate to colleagues/clients. C is grammatically OK but wordier and less idiomatic for a workplace exit.

contrast_examples.jp: 本日は直帰させていただきます。

prompt.context_jp: Haruko finally reveals her credential to the factory.
prompt.prompt_en: Which self-introduction sounds most natural and professional?

choices.text: 気象予報士の大前春子です
大前春子は気象予報士です
私の名前は大前春子、気象予報士をやっています

feedback.correct_en: The 〜の〜です pattern ('[role] + [name] + です') is the standard way to introduce yourself with a title/qualification.
feedback.incorrect_en: B sounds like describing a third party. C is grammatically possible but wordy and less polished than the title-first standard form.

prompt.context_jp: The president must decline a last-minute order of 300 extra bentos.
prompt.prompt_en: Which response sounds most natural for softly declining in business Japanese?

choices.text: 急なお願いなのは 分かっています… さらに追加で300個は…
300個は作れないと思います、たぶん

feedback.correct_en: Trailing off with 〜は… lets the listener infer refusal without blunt rejection — the hallmark of soft Japanese business refusal.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is far too blunt for a client-facing call. C mixes hedging with casual たぶん, which sounds unprofessional in a business setting.

prompt.context_jp: Satonaka and crew finish loading the last box just in time.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'we just barely made it'?

choices.text: 何とか間に合いましたね
どうにか時間に着きましたね
時間に合うことができましたね

feedback.correct_en: 何とか間に合う is the idiomatic collocation for 'barely made the deadline.' 間に合う itself means 'be in time.'
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses 時間に着く which is non-idiomatic — 着く is for arriving at places, not times. C is grammatical but stilted; 間に合う already conveys this meaning.

prompt.context_jp: Konatsu talks about trying to improve herself.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'raise my own value'?

choices.text: 自分の価値を高めなきゃ
自分の価値を大きくしなきゃ
自分の価値を増やさなきゃ

feedback.correct_en: 価値を高める ('raise/elevate one's value') is the standard collocation for self-improvement in a career context.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大きくする and 増やす don't collocate well with 価値 — they treat value as physical size or countable quantity, which sounds off.
